calls.head: Where the Devils have the edge: the power play
calls.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for the power play, and the Kings are around the middle. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one. These two rarely give each other power plays, so special teams may not get much of a say.

calls.plain: The Devils made the better chances on the power play, as the gap between these two suggested, but the goals came out even. On the scoreboard: New Jersey 0 for 2, Los Angeles 0 for 2 on the power play.
calls.said: the Devils’ power play would make more chances than the Kings’
calls.beyond: New Jersey kills penalties better than most. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: Los Angeles’s power play created 0.0 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.1 (about 6.6 against New Jersey) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 200 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Devils squeak past the Kings
paras: The Devils didn’t get their first shot on goal until late in the first, more than 16 minutes into the game. The Kings went just over 16 minutes without a shot on goal, from midway through the first to midway through the second, while the Devils put eleven on net. Scott Laughton opened the scoring for the Kings late in the second, but they didn’t score again. Anthony Mantha tied it 1-1 for New Jersey less than three minutes later, and Brett Pesce put the Devils ahead for good midway through the third. Arseny Gritsyuk sealed it into the empty net with just over a minute left.

The Devils carried the play, outshooting the Kings 26-13, and got the result to match. Jake Allen needed only 12 saves for the Devils, and Anton Forsberg kept the Kings in it, stopping 23 of 25. By our Swing measure, Luke Evangelista had the best night of anyone. The Devils improved to 7-4-0 and climbed to third in the Metropolitan, while the Kings fell to 2-5-2, slipping to seventh in the Pacific.
